questions.q: After resp = requests.get(url, timeout=10), which expression parses a JSON response body into Python lists and dictionaries?
options: resp.status_code
resp.json()
resp.timeout
pd.read_csv(resp)
questions.explain: The json() method parses the response body. status_code is only the numeric result of the request.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the timeout argument in requests.get(url, timeout=10)?
options: It limits how many rows are returned
It stops your code from waiting forever if the server does not respond
It makes the API faster
It sets how long the data stays cached
questions.explain: Without a timeout, a stalled server can leave your script hanging indefinitely.

questions.q: A response comes back with status code 404 and you call raise_for_status(). What happens?
options: It retries the request automatically
It converts the response to a DataFrame
Nothing; it only raises on status 200
It raises an HTTPError, so the failure is loud instead of silently continuing
questions.explain: raise_for_status raises requests.HTTPError for 4xx and 5xx responses, which stops a loop instead of letting bad responses slip through.

questions.q: An API returns 10 records per page. Which approach builds one DataFrame from three pages?
options: Loop over the pages, build a DataFrame per page, and combine them with pd.concat
Call resp.json() once and hope it includes every page
Call pd.merge on the URL strings
Use dropna() on the first page
questions.explain: Collect each page in a list and concatenate. The lesson's three pages of ten posts produced a (30, 4) DataFrame.

questions.q: What is the safest way to handle an API key in a notebook you might share?
options: Paste it into a code cell so the notebook is self-contained
Put it in the URL query string of every request
Read it from an environment variable such as os.environ["API_TOKEN"]
Save it inside the DataFrame
questions.explain: Keys hard-coded in notebooks are easily leaked. Environment variables keep secrets out of the code and out of version control.
